title: Finite dimensional normed spaces over complete fields are complete
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] complete for a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative absolute value satisfying the triangle inequality. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space admitting a finite basis, with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying definiteness, $\|-v\|=\|v\|$, $\|v+w\|\leq\|v\|+\|w\|$ and $\|cv\|=|c|\|v\|$. Then $V$ is complete for the metric $\|v-w\|$: every Cauchy sequence in this metric converges in $V$. The zero vector space is included.
